chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Hammad ibn 'Uthman, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, that Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

It is for them to pass by Al-Medina, so they would greet upon Rasool-Allah (peace be upon him and his family) from nearby, even though the Blessings do reach him (peace be upon him and his family) from afar.

key_terms.السَّلَامُ: Greeting, specifically the Islamic greeting of peace used in Ziyarah.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Blessings or prayers, referring to the divine blessings that reach the Prophet.
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: The city of Medina, specifically referring to the burial place of the Prophet.
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: The Messenger of Allah, referring to Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family).

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on greeting the Prophet when passing by Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the protocol for Ziyarah al-Nabi, emphasizing that while spiritual greetings (salawat) transcend distance, physical proximity in Medina is preferred for the ritual greeting. It reflects the Shia scholarly view of the Prophet’s continued spiritual presence (hayat al-barzakh) and the merit of visiting his grave as an act of devotion. The instruction underscores the importance of intention and location in enhancing the spiritual experience of the visitor.
